paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa, called Govinda, is the supreme Lord; his form is being, consciousness and bliss; he is without beginning, the beginning of all, the cause of all causes.

original.text: īśvaraḥ paramaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sac-cid-ānanda-vigrahaḥ | anādir ādir govindaḥ sarva-kāraṇa-kāraṇam ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: I worship Govinda, the primeval person, tending the wish-fulfilling cows in abodes of wish-fulfilling gems surrounded by wish-fulfilling trees, served with reverence by hundreds of thousands of goddesses of fortune.
Govinda, the soul of all, dwells in Goloka itself with those (gopīs) who are his own forms and potencies, imbued with rasa of bliss and consciousness.
notes: Jīva cites this verse ('nija-rūpatayā kalābhiḥ') for the gopīs' being his own potencies.

paraphrase: The saints, their eyes of devotion anointed with the salve of love, always see him within their hearts: Śyāmasundara, of inconceivable qualities.
The undifferentiated, infinite, complete Brahman, differentiated into the glories of countless universes, is the effulgence of his body — I worship Govinda.
Durgā — the one power that accomplishes creation, maintenance and dissolution — sustains the worlds like his shadow and acts according to his will: I worship Govinda, the primal Person.

original.text: सृष्टिस्थितिप्रलयसाधनशक्तिरेका छायेव यस्य भुवनानि विभर्त्ति दुर्गा। इच्छानुरूपमपि यस्य च चेष्टते सा गोविन्दमादिपुरुषं तमहं भजामि॥
original.edition: eBhāratī-sampat Brahmasaṃhitā with Jīva Gosvāmin's commentary (numbered 53 there)
original.licence: pre-modern text (public domain); e-text for reference

notes: Commonly numbered 5.44; Jīva's commentary elsewhere cites 'yaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ saiva durgā' and explains Durgā as Kṛṣṇa's own power, non-different from him. paraphrase: The lords of the universes, born from the pores of Mahāviṣṇu's body, live for the duration of one of his exhalations; that Mahāviṣṇu is a portion of a portion of Govinda.
